question.prompt: When \(7\) fair standard \(6\)-sided dice are thrown, the probability that the sum of the numbers on the top faces is \(10\) can be written as \[\dfrac{n}{6^{7}},\] where \(n\) is a positive integer. What is \(n?\)

solutions.title: Count the three possible patterns
solutions.explanation:
Seven dice showing 1 would have sum \(7\), so a sum of \(10\) requires exactly \(3\) extra points. Those extra points can be split only as \(3\), \(2+1\), or \(1+1+1\).

Label the dice so that different assignments to them count as different outcomes.

1. One die shows 4 and the other six show 1. Choose the die showing 4 in \(7\) ways.
2. One die shows 3, one shows 2, and the other five show 1. Choose the die showing 3, then the die showing 2, in \(7\cdot6=42\) ways.
3. Three dice show 2 and the other four show 1. Choose the three dice in
\[
\binom{7}{3}=\frac{7\cdot6\cdot5}{3\cdot2\cdot1}=35
\]
ways.

These cases cover every split of the three extra points and have different face-value patterns, so they do not overlap. Within each case, the selected dice determine exactly one outcome.

All \(6^7\) ordered outcomes are equally likely, so
\[
\Pr(\text{sum }10)=\frac{7+42+35}{6^7}=\frac{84}{6^7}.
\]
Therefore \(n=\boxed{84}\), choice E.
